heading.en: Grown-ups are not what they seem

hook.en: *Adults* tell children to be kind, honest and loving. What happens when a child notices that adults do not always do so themselves?

objectives.en: Discuss how this discovery affects a child

narration.en: Adults tell children to be kind, honest and loving. What happens when a child notices that adults do not always do so themselves?

title.en: Discuss how this discovery affects a child

say.en: Adults tell children to be kind, honest and loving. What happens when a child notices that adults do not always do so themselves? In this lesson: Explain the second possibility.
Understand the meaning of hypocrisy.
Discuss how this discovery affects a child.

body.en: In the second *stanza*, the speaker wonders whether childhood ended when he realised that adults were not all they appeared to be. They talked of love and preached it, but did not act so lovingly themselves. This gap between their words and their actions is hypocrisy. Seeing it, the child loses his innocent trust in grown-ups.

points.en: *Adults* preach love but do not always practise it
The child begins to see through appearances

problem.en: How did the hypocrisy of adults lead to the loss of the speaker's childhood?

steps.en: As a child he trusted adults completely.
He saw that they preached love but did not act lovingly.
This broke his innocent trust and made him see the world more critically.

answer.en: The speaker had trusted adults fully. When he noticed that they preached love but did not practise it, he realised they were not what they seemed. Losing his innocent trust was a step out of childhood.
